questions.answer: The value 7 appears most often, so the mode is $7$.

questions.q: Find the range of the data set $22,18,35,9,27$.
Find the interquartile range (IQR) of $4,7,9,12,15,18,21$.
questions.answer: Lower half (excluding the median 12): $4,7,9$, so $Q_1=7$. Upper half: $15,18,21$, so $Q_3=18$. IQR $=18-7=11$.
questions.explanation: Lower half (excluding the median 12): $4,7,9$, so $Q_1=7$. Upper half: $15,18,21$, so $Q_3=18$. IQR $=18-7=11$.

sections.heading: Part III — Free-Response Questions (FRQs): Challenging & Cross-Lesson Synthesis (15–20)

questions.q: The bar graph shows the results of rolling a fair die 40 times. Based on the experimental data, find the experimental probability of rolling a 4, and compare it to the theoretical probability.
questions.answer: Experimental $P(4)=\frac{9}{40}=0.225$. Theoretical $P(4)=\frac{1}{6}\approx0.167$. The experimental probability is somewhat higher than the theoretical probability, which is expected random variation in a finite sample.
questions.explanation: Experimental $P(4)=\frac{9}{40}=0.225$. Theoretical $P(4)=\frac{1}{6}\approx0.167$. The experimental probability is somewhat higher than the theoretical probability, which is expected random variation in a finite sample.

questions.q: A game costs 2 dollars to play. A player wins 10 dollars with probability 0.1, and wins nothing otherwise. Find the expected net profit per play.
questions.answer: Expected winnings $=0.1\times10=1$ dollar. Expected net profit $=1-2=-1$ dollar (an expected loss of 1 dollar per play).
questions.explanation: Expected winnings $=0.1\times10=1$ dollar. Expected net profit $=1-2=-1$ dollar (an expected loss of 1 dollar per play).

This question has three parts. A researcher surveys 200 students about whether they play a sport and whether they play a musical instrument. Of the 200 students, 120 play a sport, 80 play an instrument, and 30 do both. (a) Find how many students do neither activity. (b) Find the probability that a randomly chosen student plays a sport or an instrument (or both). (c) Given that a randomly selected student plays a sport, find the probability that they also play an instrument.
questions.target: A well-designed word problem: a survey of students
questions.answer: (a) By inclusion-exclusion, the number doing at least one activity is $120+80-30=170$. Neither $=200-170=30$. (b) $P(\mathrm{sport\ or\ instrument})=\frac{170}{200}=0.85$. (c) $P(\mathrm{instrument}\mid\mathrm{sport})=\frac{P(\mathrm{both})}{P(\mathrm{sport})}=\frac{30}{120}=\frac{1}{4}$.
questions.explanation: (a) By inclusion-exclusion, the number doing at least one activity is $120+80-30=170$. Neither $=200-170=30$. (b) $P(\mathrm{sport\ or\ instrument})=\frac{170}{200}=0.85$. (c) $P(\mathrm{instrument}\mid\mathrm{sport})=\frac{P(\mathrm{both})}{P(\mathrm{sport})}=\frac{30}{120}=\frac{1}{4}$.

The mean of five numbers is $24$. When a sixth number is added, the mean becomes $26$. What is the sixth number?
questions.answer: Sum of 5 numbers $= 5 \times 24 = 120$. Sum of 6 numbers $= 6 \times 26 = 156$. Sixth number $= 156 - 120 = 36$.
questions.explanation: Sum of 5 numbers $= 5 \times 24 = 120$. Sum of 6 numbers $= 6 \times 26 = 156$. Sixth number $= 156 - 120 = 36$.

questions.q: An outlier is defined as any data point greater than $Q_3 + 1.5 \times \mathrm{IQR}$. If $Q_1 = 20$ and $Q_3 = 35$, which value is considered an outlier?
questions.answer: $\mathrm{IQR} = 35 - 20 = 15$. Upper threshold $= 35 + 1.5(15) = 35 + 22.5 = 57.5$. Since $60 > 57.5$, $60$ is an outlier.
questions.explanation: $\mathrm{IQR} = 35 - 20 = 15$. Upper threshold $= 35 + 1.5(15) = 35 + 22.5 = 57.5$. Since $60 > 57.5$, $60$ is an outlier.

questions.q: Which change will increase the standard deviation of a dataset?
choices: Subtracting the mean from each data point
questions.answer: Multiplying by $2$ doubles the dispersion and doubles the standard deviation. Adding/subtracting a constant shifts the data without affecting standard deviation.
questions.explanation: Multiplying by $2$ doubles the dispersion and doubles the standard deviation. Adding/subtracting a constant shifts the data without affecting standard deviation.

questions.q: If $P(A) = 0.5$, $P(B) = 0.6$, and $P(A \cup B) = 0.8$, what is $P(A \cap B)$?
questions.answer: $P(A \cup B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A \cap B) \Rightarrow 0.8 = 0.5 + 0.6 - P(A \cap B) \Rightarrow P(A \cap B) = 1.1 - 0.8 = 0.3$.
questions.explanation: $P(A \cup B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A \cap B) \Rightarrow 0.8 = 0.5 + 0.6 - P(A \cap B) \Rightarrow P(A \cap B) = 1.1 - 0.8 = 0.3$.

questions.q: How many distinct $3$-person executive committees (President, Vice-President, Treasurer) can be elected from a club of $10$ members?
questions.answer: Since roles are distinct, order matters (permutation): $P(10, 3) = 10 \times 9 \times 8 = 720$.
questions.explanation: Since roles are distinct, order matters (permutation): $P(10, 3) = 10 \times 9 \times 8 = 720$.
